newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore refiners optimise diesel output over jet.
newsitem.headline: Singapore refiners optimise diesel output over jet.

text.p: Singapore refiners are producing more gas oil (diesel) at the expense of jet-kerosene fuel as prices of prompt gas oil outpaced jet values, industry sources said on Thursday.
"It does not make sense to maximise jet production as I'm out a dollar for every barrel produced," one source at a refinery said.
In the physical market, gas oil is currently priced on average at about 90 cents per barrel above jet fuel for prompt cargoes, the source said. Jet fuel values are normally higher than gas oil.
But this sharp differential in physical cargoes was not repeated in the swaps market where the April jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) traded earlier in the day at 25 cents in favour of jet fuel.
"The regrade is still positive in the swaps market because the physical gas oil is being artificially held up," one trader said.
Physical gas oil prices had since the start of this month risen by almost $3.00 per barrel following large purchases by a Singapore trader.
The local trader had over this period bought more than three million barrels of gas oil.
"Once the trader withdraws from the market we should see a $1.00-$1.50 per barrel downward correction to gas oil prices," the source said.
Refiners are currently switching their production mode to maximise gas oil output to take advantage of the steep price differential.
The refiners have the flexibility at the refining stage to dump about 10-20 percent of the jet fuel cut into the gas oil pool.
In addition to this, they can also blend another 10-20 percent of jet fuel into the gas oil pool depending on the flash point of the gas oil sought.
If the flash point, the temperature at which the fuel ignites, is low then they can blend more jet fuel into the gas oil, the source said.
Traders said such a sharp negative regrade is not seen in the swaps market as it was still reflecting the fundamentals where the last vestiges of the winter jet fuel buying was still seen.
"It is too early to say if the regrade would turn negative in the second quarter as there are still committments to be covered," another refining source.
He said that surplus physical jet fuel should be entering the market sometime in mid-April.
Traditionally, the second quarter sees a negative regrade in line with a period of low demand for jet fuel as it is no longer required for heating in north Asia.
But at the moment, the second quarter regrade was last quoted at plus 20/40 cents, brokers said.
